title: Credit-based ring pacer and async NCCL progress + KV-cache sharding for TP runtime
author: Evan Brooks
description: Motivation: TP inference workloads with imbalanced micro-batches frequently hit transient NCCL stalls and KV-cache thrashing when multiple tensor slices contend for allreduce bandwidth. This PR introduces a credit-based ring pacer that smooths outgoing collective launches, an asynchronous NCCL progress helper to reduce kernel blocking in user threads, and a lightweight KV-cache sharding layer to reduce lock contention for hot prefixes. Scope: runtime/tp scheduler and comm stack, small API surface for ops to observe credits, and tests/benchmarks. Changes include a new credit allocator, pacing hooks in the TP dispatcher, an async-progress thread with cooperative polling, and a KV cache shard map with per-shard mutexing and eviction heuristics. Checklist: - Add credit pacer and integrate into TP dispatcher - Implement async NCCL progress and graceful shutdown - Introduce KV-cache sharding and eviction policy tuned for short sequences - Add microbench harness and end-to-end regression test for 8xA100 TP scenarios - Ensure CI and perf traces show regression-free latency and improved p99 throughput Results summary: internal perf runs on 8xA100 reduced end-to-end token p99 by ~18% on a mixed short/long prompt workload and reduced collective queuing stalls visible in tracing. KV-cache hit rates increased on hot-prefix traces by ~12% and per-prefix lock contention is eliminated in the common case. Backwards compatibility: no API changes for customers; runtime knobs exposed via config flags (credit_initial, shard_count, async_progress=true). Rollout plan: staged canary on Dedicated pools; opt-in by default for new Dedicated clusters, off by default for older clusters until nightly perf validation completes. Notes on stability: async progress thread has a conservative polling backoff; integrated with existing shutdown flow to avoid leaks. Referenced issues/threads: Linear ENG-9241 describes production incidents where mixed sequence workloads regressed after recent batching changes; SUP-4482 is the support ticket requesting relief for a customer on Dedicated.

review_conversation:
Hannah Chen: Can you explain why we need a new thread for NCCL progress vs. using the kernel poll hooks?
Evan: Kernel hooks introduced measurable scheduling jitter for busy application threads; async thread decouples progress from user work and reduces preemption. Polling is cooperative and disabled for low-load.
Diego: Please add a config knob and validate shutdown races.
Evan: Added runtime flag async_progress=true/false and added join/timeout logic in the shutdown path (see nccl_progress.cc).
Priya: Are there memory/CPU costs for the shard map? How did you pick shard_count default?
Evan: Shard_count defaults to number of worker threads / 4 with a floor of 4; memory overhead is small (per-shard unordered_map) and we guard heavy workloads with an adaptive eviction threshold. Added microbench results to the PR description.
Hannah: Approve after tests are green—please add a short doc note describing operational knobs.
Evan: Added docs/ops/credit_pacer.md describing knobs, expected behavior, and debugging guidance.
Final: LGTM, approved by Hannah and Diego.
release_notes: Improved multi-GPU TP runtime stability and latency: credit-based ring pacing, async NCCL progress helper, and KV-cache sharding reduce collective contention and cache lock hotspots. Exposed runtime knobs: credit_initial, credit_refill_ms, shard_count, async_progress.
notes: Deployed to canary Dedicated pools for 48h with no regressions; monitoring dashboards updated (route:tp/collectives/credit_pacer). Follow-up work: iterate on credit refill heuristics (ENG-9310) and add telemetry to measure per-shard eviction counters.
